title: Unique Splitting For Prime-To-Z Compact Subgroups
body_html:
Unique Splitting For Prime-To-Z Compact Subgroups

Let

$$ 1\to Z\to \widetilde G\to G\to 1 $$

be a $Z$-cover. If $H\subset G$ is compact and

$$ |H|\wedge |Z|=1, $$

then the draft asserts that there is a unique group homomorphism

$$ \iota_H:H\to \widetilde H $$

which is a section of $\widetilde H\to H$. In particular,

$$ \widetilde H\simeq H\times Z $$

as topological groups.

Draft Caution

The TeX proof gives two sketches: one via vanishing of group cohomology and one via exactness of invariants. The conclusion is intended as a reusable input for comparing genuine cover representations with ordinary representations on prime-to-$Z$ compact subgroups.
